items.title: Finite simplicial constructible sheaves have an actual derived incidence model
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $K$ be a finite simplicial complex, $D$ a subcomplex and $X=|K|\setminus|D|$. Let $P$ be the face poset of the open simplices of $K$ not in $D$, ordered by inclusion of faces. The exact realization of finite-dimensional covariant $k$-diagrams on $P$ induces a fully faithful functor into $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$, with essential image the complexes having bounded finite-rank locally constant cohomology on each open simplex. Ordinary and compact-support cohomology, ordinary Hom and internal derived Hom have bounded finite cochain models and commute with every coefficient field extension. For a local product projection $\operatorname{pr}:V\times F\to V$ with supplied finite deleted-boundary models, there is a natural local comparison $R\operatorname{pr}_*\operatorname{pr}^*B\simeq B\otimes_k C^*(F;k)$, taking the unit to $B\otimes(k\to C^*(F;k))$. This does not assert that an arbitrary algebraic map is simplicial.
items.strategy:
Route (Goresky, Lecture Notes on Sheaves and Perverse Sheaves, §2.1-§2.5 and §32.2: simplicial sheaves, elementary injectives and the simplicial derived equivalence; Bernstein-Lunts, Equivariant Sheaves and Functors, Part I §1.9 and Appendix A for the acyclic-comparison technique).
Step 1 (ordinary incidence equivalence). Give $P$ the Alexandrov topology of upward-closed sets; the carrier map $q:X\to P$ taking a point to its open simplex is continuous because the preimage of the principal filter $P_{\ge\sigma}$ is the open star $\operatorname{St}(\sigma)$ ([[def-simplicial-subcomplex-star-closure-and-link]]), and $X$ is open in the compact Hausdorff space $|K|$ ([[prop-a-finite-simplicial-complex-has-compact-hausdorff-realization]], [[def-geometric-realization-of-an-abstract-simplicial-complex]]). A covariant finite-dimensional diagram on $P$ is a sheaf on $P$ with stalk $V_\sigma$ and generization maps, and the exact inverse image $q^*$ ([[def-inverse-image-presheaf-and-sheaf]], [[lem-stalk-inverse-image-sheaf]]) realizes it as an actual sheaf whose restriction to each open simplex is constant with value $V_\sigma$. Conversely, a sheaf that is locally constant of finite rank on each open simplex ([[def-locally-constant-sheaf-of-finite-rank]]) is recovered by parallel transport along the contractible, simply connected simplices: define $F_\sigma\to F_\tau$ for $\sigma\le\tau$ by restricting a representative germ and transporting along a path in $\tau$, prove independence of representatives and of paths and the transitivity equation, and conclude with the stalkwise isomorphism criterion ([[def-stalk-of-presheaf]], [[thm-sheaf-morphism-isomorphism-stalkwise]]). The ordinary realization is exact because exactness is stalkwise ([[thm-exactness-of-sheaves-stalkwise]]). This step is the standard triviality of a locally constant sheaf on a contractible, simply connected space and is written out inline; it is the only place where simple connectivity of the simplices is used.
Step 2 (diagram injectives and their realizations). For $\tau\in P$ and finite-dimensional $W$ define the diagram $I_\tau(W)$ with value $W$ at every $\sigma\le\tau$ and $0$ elsewhere, the maps being identities where defined; a diagram map $V\to I_\tau(W)$ is precisely a linear map $V_\tau\to W$, so $I_\tau(W)$ is injective, and $V$ embeds into $\bigoplus_\tau I_\tau(V_\tau)$. Finiteness of $P$ and the finite-poset bar bound ([[lem-finite-poset-diagrams-have-bounded-finite-bar-models]]) give finite injective and, dually, finite projective resolutions with explicit chain-length bounds. Realized injectives are closed pushforwards: $q^*I_\tau(W)=i_{\tau*}\bigl(W_{|\tau|\setminus|D|}\bigr)$ for the closed inclusion $i_\tau$ ([[lem-sheaf-supported-on-a-closed-subset-is-a-pushforward]], [[def-direct-image-sheaf]], [[lem-direct-image-is-sheaf]]), and closed pushforward is exact and preserves injectives because its left adjoint is exact ([[thm-inverse-direct-image-adjunction]]).
Step 3 (star and simplex acyclicity). For an open star $V=\operatorname{St}(\sigma)$ the closed-immersion cohomology comparison ([[lem-closed-immersion-preserves-sheaf-cohomology]], [[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]) identifies $R\Gamma\bigl(V,q^*I_\tau(W)\bigr)$ with $R\Gamma\bigl(V\cap(|\tau|\setminus|D|),W\bigr)$; that intersection is empty or star-convex in $\tau$ and contracts radially to the barycenter of $\sigma$, so the constant-polyhedral comparison ([[lem-locally-contractible-metric-spaces-have-singular-constant-sheaf-cohomology]]) gives $W$ in degree $0$ and nothing in positive degrees. Hence $R\Gamma(\operatorname{St}(\sigma),q^*V)=V_\sigma$ concentrated in degree $0$, and the realized injective resolution really computes cohomology on stars and on $X$.
Step 4 (derived full faithfulness and essential image). Realized diagram projectives are $q^*P_\sigma=j_!\bigl(k_{\operatorname{St}(\sigma)}\bigr)$, and extension by zero with the cohomology-as-derived-morphisms identification gives $R\mathcal{H}om_X(q^*P_\sigma,q^*V)=R\Gamma(\operatorname{St}(\sigma),q^*V)=V_\sigma$ in degree $0$ ([[def-extension-by-zero-abelian-sheaf]], [[thm-extension-by-zero-adjunction-exactness]], [[lem-sheaf-cohomology-classes-as-derived-morphisms]], [[def-derived-hom-in-the-bounded-setting]]). The explicit finite bar resolution over strict chains with coefficient maps ([[lem-finite-poset-diagrams-have-bounded-finite-bar-models]]) therefore identifies the actual derived Hom of realized bounded complexes with the finite matrix complex of the diagram derived Hom; this is full faithfulness ([[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]], [[lem-field-module-sheaves-have-injective-derived-models]]). Essential image: Step 1 realizes each cohomology sheaf of a complex with bounded finite-rank locally constant cohomology on each simplex, and the finite canonical truncation triangles let the connecting morphisms and the successive cones be realized by induction ([[def-canonical-truncation-of-a-complex]], [[thm-canonical-truncations-fit-a-distinguished-triangle]], [[thm-the-derived-category-inherits-a-triangulated-structure]]). No injectives among all analytic sheaves are claimed to be constructible.
Step 5 (compact supports). The resolution terms are also c-soft/Γ_c-acyclic in the required sense, and compact-support cohomology of the model is computed by the finite relative cochains $(|\tau|,|\tau|\cap|D|)$ through the compact-support calculus ([[lem-c-soft-field-sheaves-are-compact-support-acyclic]], [[def-compactly-supported-global-sections]]).
Step 6 (internal derived Hom). Restrict the injective Hom model to a small polyhedral neighbourhood of a point of an open simplex; open restriction preserves injectives because its exact left adjoint is extension by zero ([[thm-extension-by-zero-adjunction-exactness]], [[def-restriction-sheaf-open-subspace]]). The restricted complexes are finite, and affine product charts along the simplex identify them as the point moves, so internal derived Hom has locally constant finite-dimensional stalks and uniform finite local models ([[def-sheaf-hom]]).
Step 7 (local product comparison). For $\operatorname{pr}:V\times F\to V$ choose finite deleted-boundary cell models on the base chart and on $F$, and tensor a finite diagram-injective resolution of the base diagram with the constant fiber diagram on the product cell complex. The terms are supported on products of closed cells minus their deleted boundary; their cohomology on a base star times a fiber cell is $k$ in degree $0$ by the same constant-polyhedral comparison, and the resulting cochain complex is the tensor product of the base evaluation complex with $C^*(F;k)$ ([[cor-kunneth-over-a-field]]). The comparison maps agree with restriction and the inverse/direct-image adjunction, giving $R\operatorname{pr}_*\operatorname{pr}^*B\simeq B\otimes_k C^*(F;k)$ with unit $B\otimes(k\to C^*(F;k))$; if $H^1\dots H^r$ of $F$ vanish the cone lies in $D^{\ge b+r+1}$ for $B$ in $D^{\ge b}$.
Step 8 (coefficient fields). Tensoring with an exact field extension commutes with all finite sums, kernels, images and comparison matrices used in Steps 2-7, which yields the stated scalar comparison for ordinary and compact-support cohomology and for ordinary and internal derived Hom.
Caveats. Only finite diagrams and finite complexes occur; no finite-dimensionality of arbitrary sections of arbitrary sheaves and no simpliciality of an arbitrary algebraic map is claimed. AC is consumed only through the injective-model supplier ([[lem-field-module-sheaves-have-injective-derived-models]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]); the remaining constructions are finite or choice-free. The authored proof must write out the parallel-transport triviality of Step 1 and the finite double-complex computation of Step 7 in full; only the route is offered here.
items.axiom_use: AC is assumed and consumed through [[lem-field-module-sheaves-have-injective-derived-models]] (functorial injective replacements, products of injectives) and the choice-dependent sheaf-cohomology suppliers [[lem-closed-immersion-preserves-sheaf-cohomology]] and [[lem-sheaf-cohomology-classes-as-derived-morphisms]]; all remaining constructions are finite or choice-free.

items.title: Locally split Cech nerves give actual derived Cartesian sheaf descent
items.statement: Assume AC. For a strict augmented simplicial space $Z_\bullet\to S$, its category of simplicial analytic $k$-sheaves has explicit coinduced injective resolutions. The derived augmentation is computed by the normalized double complex with first page $R^j q_{p*}F_p$ and alternating face differential. A common internal lower bound makes every total-degree diagonal finite. The same construction works for strict bisimplicial diagrams and is compatible with composition of derived right adjoints to exact inverse image. If $Z_\bullet$ is the Čech nerve of a map $P\to S$ admitting local sections, inverse image gives an equivalence from $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(S))$ to the full derived subcategory with Cartesian cohomology. For algebraic principal $\mathrm{GL}$ bundles this restricts to the algebraically constructible subcategories.
items.strategy:
Route (Bernstein-Lunts, Equivariant Sheaves and Functors, Part I: Appendix B1-B6 for the simplicial description of the bounded derived category and the free-space model, §1.9 with Appendix A2-A4 for acyclic maps and the local-section base-change criterion, §2.1-§2.5 for the resolution categories; Goresky §2.1-§2.3 and §32.2 for the constructible simplicial model).
Step 1 (the simplicial sheaf category). A simplicial sheaf on $Z_\bullet$ is a family $F_p$ with structure maps $\alpha^*F_m\to F_p$ satisfying the composition identities; kernels, cokernels and filtered colimits are computed levelwise (cokernels after sheafification), and inverse image is exact over a field. Evaluation at $p$ is exact; its left adjoint is the free simplicial sheaf built from finite sums of inverse images along the simplicial operators and is exact because inverse images and direct sums of sheaves are exact ([[def-direct-image-sheaf]], [[lem-direct-image-is-sheaf]], [[def-inverse-image-presheaf-and-sheaf]], [[thm-inverse-direct-image-adjunction]], [[thm-exactness-of-sheaves-stalkwise]]). Its right adjoint $N_p$ is coinduction, $(N_pI)_m=\prod_{\alpha:[m]\to[p]}\alpha_*I$; direct images are right adjoints of exact inverse images, so they preserve injectives, and products of injectives are injective under AC ([[thm-a-coproduct-of-projectives-is-projective-and-a-product-of-injectives-is-injective]]). Embedding each $F_p$ into an ordinary injective $I_p$ ([[lem-field-module-sheaves-have-injective-derived-models]]) therefore gives enough injectives and an explicit objectwise resolution; levelwise kernels/colimits give local smallness and AB5, so the bounded-below derived category is an actual derived sheaf category ([[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]], [[thm-injective-complexes-model-the-bounded-below-derived-category]], [[def-cochain-complex-in-an-abelian-category]]).
Step 2 (derived augmentation). For $N_pI$ the cosimplicial sheaf $m\mapsto q_{m*}(N_pI)_m$ is a product of copies of $q_{p*}I$ indexed by the $m$-simplices of the standard $p$-simplex, and inserting vertex $0$ into ordered vertex tuples gives an explicit contracting homotopy of the normalized augmented complex with augmentation $q_{p*}I$; hence the augmented complex is exact in positive degrees on injectives and the derived augmentation is computed by the normalized double complex with pages $R^jq_{p*}F_p$ and alternating face differential ([[def-direct-sum-total-complex-of-a-double-complex]], [[lem-the-total-differential-squares-to-zero]], [[thm-the-cohomological-filtered-complex-construction]], [[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]). Because the injective resolution carries a common internal lower bound and the simplicial index is nonnegative, every total-degree diagonal is finite, so the spectral sequence converges to the total complex without completion hypotheses. The strict bisimplicial case coinduces along pairs of simplicial operators; the two vertex-insertion contractions give the bidegreewise exactness, iterated and simultaneous totalizations agree on finite diagonals, and composition of derived right adjoints to exact inverse images is compatible with the construction.
Step 3 (Čech descent). If $Z_\bullet$ is the Čech nerve of $q:P\to S$ admitting local sections, then on a local section the rows $R^jq_{m*}q_m^*B$ carry a contracting homotopy obtained by inserting the section, and the already-constructed augmentation spectral sequence for $q^*B$ collapses to give $B\cong Rq_*q^*B$; finite truncation triangles extend this to all bounded complexes and the derived adjunction proves full faithfulness ([[def-canonical-truncation-of-a-complex]], [[thm-canonical-truncations-fit-a-distinguished-triangle]], [[thm-the-derived-category-inherits-a-triangulated-structure]]). The essential image is the full derived subcategory of objects with Cartesian cohomology: ordinary descent glues the local sheaves on a local section along the Cartesian isomorphism on $P\times_SP$, whose degree-two cocycle is the simplicial identity, and conversely $q^*$ of a complex on $S$ is Cartesian. A bounded Cartesian complex is built from its descended cohomology sheaves by truncation triangles, and full faithfulness lifts the connecting morphisms, so the induction closes.
Step 4 (algebraic constructibility). On finite algebraic graph charts with algebraic transition maps the descended bounded complex is algebraically constructible in the sense of [[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]; no naive equivariant abelian category for a nonfree action, and no general proper-descent theorem, is claimed.
Caveats. The general total model of Steps 1-2 uses neither the Čech hypothesis nor local sections; the local-section hypothesis is used only in Step 3. AC enters through products of injectives and the injective-replacement machinery ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). [[thm-extension-by-zero-adjunction-exactness]] is retained from the design's declared inputs as an ambient exactness/adjunction supplier; the present route does not visibly load it, so Step 3 must either exhibit an explicit open-subspace use or record it as a declared input that is not used (the lemma's statement and scope are unchanged). The authored proof must supply the explicit coinduced resolutions and the contracting homotopies in full and must not cite proper hypercover descent.
items.axiom_use: AC is assumed and consumed through [[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[lem-field-module-sheaves-have-injective-derived-models]] and [[thm-a-coproduct-of-projectives-is-projective-and-a-product-of-injectives-is-injective]] (products of injectives, injective replacements). The simplicial and descent constructions are otherwise choice-free.

title: Constructible Incidence And Cochain Models Examples

items.title: Incidence cochains of a closed interval
items.statement:
Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Stratify the closed interval by its endpoints and open edge. A finite constructible sheaf has vector spaces $V_0,V_1,V_e$ with generization maps $u_0:V_0\to V_e$ and $u_1:V_1\to V_e$. Its actual derived global sections are computed by
$$[V_0\oplus V_1\xrightarrow{u_0-u_1}V_e],$$
in degrees zero and one. Thus a constant sheaf $k$ has cohomology $k$ in degree zero and zero otherwise. Extension by zero of $k$ on the open edge has one copy of $k$ in degree one and zero otherwise.
items.strategy: Direct verification of the incidence model on the three open simplices. The strict face chains have length at most one (the two nonidentity arrows are $0\to e$ and $1\to e$), so the inverse-limit bar model of [[lem-finite-simplicial-constructible-sheaves-have-a-derived-incidence-model]] has degree-zero term $V_0\oplus V_1\oplus V_e$, degree-one term $V_e\oplus V_e$ and differential $(v_0,v_1,w)\mapsto(w-u_0v_0,\,w-u_1v_1)$. An invertible change of the target coordinates (subtract the second output from the first) and the corresponding invertible change of source coordinate turn this complex into the direct sum of a contractible two-term complex $t\mapsto t$ and the asserted two-term complex $[V_0\oplus V_1\xrightarrow{u_0-u_1}V_e]$; this yields the stated computation of the actual derived global sections ([[def-extension-by-zero-abelian-sheaf]], [[def-geometric-realization-of-an-abstract-simplicial-complex]]). For the constant sheaf all three vector spaces are $k$ and both generization maps are the identity, so the difference map is surjective with one-dimensional kernel; for the extension by zero of $k$ on the open edge both endpoint spaces vanish, leaving a single degree-one term ([[lem-constant-sheaf-is-the-sheaf-of-locally-constant-functions]]). The statement and verification are a worked example generated for this page (no source states this exact two-term witness); the method is the one supplied by the incidence lemma.
items.axiom_use: None beyond the AC already assumed by [[lem-finite-simplicial-constructible-sheaves-have-a-derived-incidence-model]]; the computation itself is finite linear algebra.
